# jplot

Jplot tracks expvar-like (JSON) metrics and plot their evolution over time right into your iTerm2, Kitty terminal, or terminals with DRCS Sixel Graphics support.

![](doc/demo.gif)

Above capture is jplot monitoring a Go service's expvar:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars \
    memstats.HeapSys+memstats.HeapAlloc+memstats.HeapIdle+marker,counter:memstats.NumGC \
    counter:memstats.TotalAlloc \
    memstats.HeapObjects \
    memstats.StackSys+memstats.StackInuse
```

By default, jplot uses the full size of the terminal, but it is possible to limit the render to a few rows:

![](doc/rows.gif)

## Install

Using homebrew:

```
brew install rs/tap/jplot
```

This tool works with [iTerm2](https://www.iterm2.com), [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/), [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/), or terminals that support DRCS Sixel Graphics.

## Usage

Given the following JSON output:

```
{
    "mem": {
        "Heap": 1234,
        "Sys": 4321,
        "Stack": 203
    },
    "cpu": {
        "STime": 123,
        "UTime":1234
    },
    "Threads": 2
}
```

You can graph the number of thread over time:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars Threads
```

![](doc/single.png)

Or create a graph with both Utime and Stime growth rate on the same axis by using `+` between two field paths:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars counter:cpu.STime+counter:cpu.UTime
```

Note: the `counter:` prefix instructs jplot to compute the difference between the values instead of showing their absolute value.

![](doc/dual.png)


Or create several graphs by providing groups of fields as separate arguments; each argument creates a new graph:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars mem.Heap+mem.Sys+mem.Stack counter:cpu.STime+cpu.UTime Threads
```

![](doc/all.png)

### Spec Syntax

Each positional arguments given to jplot create a stacked graph with the specified values. To reference the values, use JSON query syntax. Several value paths can be referenced for the same graph by using the `+` character to separate them.

In addition, each value path can be prefixed with options separated from the path by a column. Several options can be used for the same command by separating them with a comma like so: `option1,option2:value.path`.

Supported options are:
* `counter`: Computes the difference with the last value. The value must increase monotonically.
* `marker`: When the value is none-zero, a vertical line is drawn.

## Recipes

### Memstats

Here is an example command to graph a Go program memstats:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars \
    memstats.HeapSys+memstats.HeapAlloc+memstats.HeapIdle+marker,counter:memstats.NumGC \
    counter:memstats.TotalAlloc \
    memstats.HeapObjects \
    memstats.StackSys+memstats.StackInuse
```

![](doc/memstats.png)

### Vegeta

With the help of jaggr, jplot can be used to integrate vegeta as follow:

```
echo 'GET http://localhost:8080' | \
    vegeta attack -rate 5000 -workers 100 -duration 10m | vegeta dump | \
    jaggr @count=rps \
          hist\[100,200,300,400,500\]:code \
          p25,p50,p95:latency \
          sum:bytes_in \
          sum:bytes_out | \
    jplot rps+code.hist.100+code.hist.200+code.hist.300+code.hist.400+code.hist.500 \
          latency.p95+latency.p50+latency.p25 \
          bytes_in.sum+bytes_out.sum
```

![](doc/vegeta.gif)

### Supported Terminals

* [xterm](http://invisible-island.net/xterm/)
* [iTerm2](https://www.iterm2.com/) on OSX
* [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/) on Linux/macOS/Windows
* [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/) on Linux/macOS/Windows
* [mintty](https://mintty.github.io/) on UNIX OSs via SSH
* [mlterm](https://sourceforge.net/projects/mlterm/) on Linux and Windows
* [RLogin](http://nanno.dip.jp/softlib/man/rlogin/) on Windows
* [yaft](http://uobikiemukot.github.io/yaft/) on Linux console
* [yaft-android](https://github.com/uobikiemukot/yaft-android) on Android
* [Tanasinn](http://saitoha.github.io/tanasinn/) on Firefox/Thunderbird

// Package graph renders the dashboard images.
package graph

import (
	"errors"

// Dash is a set of graphs rendered on top of each other.
type Dash struct {
	Specs []data.Spec
	Data  *data.Points
}

var palette = []color.NRGBA{
	{0, 116, 217, 255},
	{0, 217, 101, 255},
	{217, 0, 116, 255},
	{0, 217, 210, 255},
	{217, 101, 0, 255},
	{106, 195, 203, 255},
	{42, 190, 137, 255},
	{110, 128, 139, 255},
	{240, 174, 90, 255},
}

var (
	axisColor   = color.NRGBA{180, 180, 180, 255}
	legendBg    = color.NRGBA{0, 0, 0, 100}
	markerColor = color.NRGBA{110, 128, 139, 100}
	white       = color.NRGBA{255, 255, 255, 255}
)

type series struct {
	name  string
	vals  []float64
	last  float64
	color color.NRGBA
}

type graph struct {
	series  []series
	markers [][]float64
	steps   int
}

// newGraph collects the data of a single graph.
func newGraph(spec data.Spec, dp *data.Points) (*graph, error) {
	g := &graph{}
	for _, f := range spec.Fields {
		vals := dp.Get(f.ID)
		if f.Marker {
			g.markers = append(g.markers, vals)
			continue
		}
		s := series{
			name:  f.Name,
			vals:  vals,
			color: palette[len(g.series)%len(palette)],
		}
		s.last = vals[len(vals)-1]
		g.series = append(g.series, s)
	}
	if len(g.series) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("please provide at least one series")
	}
	g.steps = len(g.series[0].vals)
	if g.steps < 2 {
		return nil, errors.New("zero x-range delta; there needs to be at least (2) values")
	}
	if lo, hi := g.yRange(); math.IsInf(hi-lo, 0) {
		return nil, errors.New("infinite y-range delta")
	}
	return g, nil
}

// Render draws the dashboard as a PNG image of the given size into w.
func (d Dash) Render(w io.Writer, width, height int) error {
	graphs := make([]*graph, 0, len(d.Specs))
	for _, spec := range d.Specs {
		g, err := newGraph(spec, d.Data)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		graphs = append(graphs, g)
	}
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rectangle{Max: image.Point{X: width, Y: height}})
	c := newCanvas(img)
	n := len(graphs)
	for i, g := range graphs {
		top := float64(height) * float64(i) / float64(n)
		bottom := float64(height) * float64(i+1) / float64(n)
		pad := 11.1
		if i > 0 {
			pad = 10
		}
		g.draw(c, 0, top, float64(width), bottom, pad)
	}
	return png.Encode(w, img)
}

	lo, hi := math.Inf(1), math.Inf(-1)
	for _, s := range g.series {
		for _, v := range s.vals {

	}
	if lo == hi {
		lo -= 0.05
		hi += 0.05
	}
	return lo, hi
}

func (g *graph) draw(c *canvas, x0, y0, x1, y1 float64, topPad float64) {
	th := y1 - y0
	full := c.bounds()
	hasMarkers := g.hasMarkers()

	lo, hi := g.yRange()
	ny := int(math.Floor((th - 100) / 31.2))
	if ny < 1 {
		ny = 1
	}
	ystep := (hi - lo) / float64(ny)
	yres := tickResolution(hi - lo)
	ylabels := make([]string, ny+1)
	maxLabel := 0.0
	for i := 0; i <= ny; i++ {
		ylabels[i] = yTickLabel(lo+float64(i)*ystep, yres)
		maxLabel = math.Max(maxLabel, axisFace.width(ylabels[i]))
	}
	tags := make([]string, len(g.series))
	maxTag := 0.0
	for i, s := range g.series {
		tags[i] = humanValue(s.last)
		maxTag = math.Max(maxTag, smallFace.width(tags[i]))
	}

	right := math.Round(x1 - math.Max(maxLabel+12, maxTag+18.5))
	top := y0 + topPad
	bottom := math.Round(y1 - 26)
	if hasMarkers {
		top -= 1.5
		bottom = math.Round(y1 - 21)
	}
	xmax := float64(g.steps - 1)
	nx := int(math.Floor((x1 - x0 - 160) / 49))
	if nx < 1 {
		nx = 1
	}
	xstep := xmax / float64(nx)
	xres := tickResolution(xmax)
	left := math.Round(x0)
	if !hasMarkers {
		left = math.Round(x0 + axisFace.width(xTickLabel(0, xres))/2 - 1.6)
	}
	if right < left+3 {
		right = left + 3
	}
	if bottom < top+1 {
		bottom = top + 1
	}

	dl, dr := left+1, right-1
	px := func(i float64) float64 { return dl + (dr-dl)*i/xmax }
	py := func(v float64) float64 { return bottom - (bottom-top)*(v-lo)/(hi-lo) }
	plotClip := image.Rect(int(math.Floor(left)), int(math.Floor(top)), int(math.Ceil(right)), int(math.Ceil(bottom))+1)

	// Frame and axes.
	c.strokeLine(full, axisColor, 1, point{left, top}, point{left, bottom})
	c.strokeLine(full, axisColor, 1, point{left, bottom}, point{right, bottom})
	c.strokeLine(full, axisColor, 1, point{right, top}, point{right, bottom})

	// Y ticks and labels.
	ch := axisFace.capHeight()
	for i := 0; i <= ny; i++ {
		y := math.Round(py(lo + float64(i)*ystep))
		c.strokeLine(full, axisColor, 1, point{right, y}, point{right + tickLen, y})
		axisFace.draw(c, full, right+10, y+ch/2-0.1, axisColor, ylabels[i])
	}

	// X ticks and labels.
	if !hasMarkers {
		for i := 0; i <= nx; i++ {
			v := ceilTo(float64(i)*xstep, xres)
			if v > xmax {
				v = xmax
			}
			x := math.Ceil(px(v) - 1e-9)
			c.strokeLine(full, axisColor, 1, point{x, bottom}, point{x, bottom + tickLen})
			lbl := xTickLabel(float64(i)*xstep, xres)
			lw := axisFace.width(lbl)
			axisFace.draw(c, full, x-lw/2, bottom+20.5, axisColor, lbl)
		}
	}

	// Series: translucent area and line.
	zero := py(0)
	zero = math.Max(math.Min(zero, bottom), top)
	for _, s := range g.series {
		pts := make([]point, len(s.vals))
		for i, v := range s.vals {
			pts[i] = point{px(float64(i)), py(v)}
		}
		area := make(polygon, 0, len(pts)+2)
		area = append(area, point{pts[0].X, zero})
		area = append(area, pts...)
		area = append(area, point{pts[len(pts)-1].X, zero})
		fill := s.color
		fill.A = 20
		c.fillPolys(plotClip, fill, area)
	}
	for _, s := range g.series {
		pts := make([]point, len(s.vals))
		for i, v := range s.vals {
			pts[i] = point{px(float64(i)), py(v)}
		}
		c.strokeLine(full, s.color, 2, pts...)
	}

	// Markers: dashed vertical lines.
	for _, m := range g.markers {
		for i, v := range m {
			if v == 0 {
				continue
			}
			x := px(float64(i))
			var dashes []polygon
			for y := top + 1; y < bottom; y += 4 {
				ye := math.Min(y+2, bottom)
				dashes = append(dashes, rect(x-1, y, x+1, ye))
			}
			c.fillPolys(full, markerColor, dashes...)
		}
	}

	// Value tags.
	sch := smallFace.capHeight()
	for i, s := range g.series {
		y := py(s.last)
		tw := smallFace.width(tags[i])
		tip := right - 2
		bx0 := right + 8
		bx1 := right + 11 + tw + 4.5
		shape := polygon{{tip, y}, {bx0, y - 8}, {bx1, y - 8}, {bx1, y + 8}, {bx0, y + 8}}
		c.fillPolys(full, s.color, shape)
		smallFace.draw(c, full, right+11, y+sch/2-0.5, white, tags[i])
	}

	// Legend.
	g.drawLegend(c, left+1, math.Ceil(y0+topPad))
}

func (g *graph) drawLegend(c *canvas, x, y float64) {
	const (
		padL     = 6.0
		padR     = 10.0
		gap      = 6.0
		thumbMin = 20.0
		entryH   = 14.33
		padV     = 9.67
	)
	if len(g.series) == 0 {
		return
	}
	texts := make([]string, len(g.series))
	maxW := 0.0
	for i, s := range g.series {
		texts[i] = s.name + ":" + humanValue(s.last)
		maxW = math.Max(maxW, smallFace.width(texts[i]))
	}
	w := math.Round(padL + maxW + gap + thumbMin + padR)
	h := math.Round(padV + entryH*float64(len(g.series)))
	full := c.bounds()
	c.fillPolys(full, legendBg, rect(x, y, x+w, y+h))
	sch := smallFace.capHeight()
	for i, s := range g.series {
		cy := math.Round(y + 10 + entryH*float64(i))
		smallFace.draw(c, full, x+padL-1, cy+sch/2-0.5, axisColor, texts[i])
		tx := x + padL + smallFace.width(texts[i]) + gap
		c.fillPolys(full, s.color, rect(math.Round(tx), cy-1, x+w-padR, cy+1))
	}
}
